title: Secure Symmetric Encryption with Aggressively Reduced Algebraic Degree
summary: Filter permutators provide a low-noise, low-degree design direction, but secure symmetric encryption with aggressively reduced algebraic degree remains an open construction question.

formal_statement.body: Filter permutators are symmetric constructions that apply low-degree filtering directly to permuted key bits to obtain low homomorphic noise [S1]. Their non-standard design principles require additional cryptanalysis, including algebraic attacks that exploit sparsity in the resulting systems of equations [S1]. The unresolved construction-existence question is whether one can construct a secure symmetric encryption scheme whose algebraic degree is aggressively reduced [S1].

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography and stream-cipher design focused on filter permutators and low-noise encryption.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether one can construct a secure symmetric encryption scheme whose algebraic degree is aggressively reduced.

progress.summary: The paper presents this as the main question raised by filter permutators and notes that their non-standard design principles require additional cryptanalysis, including algebraic attacks exploiting sparsity in the resulting systems of equations.
